samples.summary: `collectStale()` is not scoped to the signed-in user and deletes other accounts' entries and archives on a shared device
samples.evidence: `collectStale` walks `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` (line 873) and `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` (line 886) with no `BY_USER` intersection, then `purge()`s each key; `orphanSnapshotKeys()` (line 892) is likewise unscoped. Every other deletion path in this file is deliberately user-scoped and the file's own comments call an unscoped scan a cross-account harm — `evictOldest` line 1034-1035 ("Only this user's entries are ours to free … the exact harm `dropAllForUser` and `listArchives` are careful to avoid"), `dropAllForUser` line 843, `listArchives` line 787, `loadArchive`'s `row.userId !== this.userId` check. The database is per-origin, so on a machine two accounts share, `OfflineRuntime` (packages/frontend/src/components/offline-runtime.tsx:69) runs `store.collectStale()` on every authenticated mount for user A and silently destroys user B's aged headers *and* B's `archives` rows — the archives being, per this feature's own design, the only remaining copy of work the SDK could not reconcile, which B would otherwise be offered back on their next session. Attacker/abuse path: any user who signs in on the device after B has been away long enough acts on B's data with no authority to do so. Fix is the same intersection `evictOldest` already performs.

samples.summary: Locally persisted document content is never purged when the user loses access to the document (workspace member removal, role change, share revocation) — only on explicit delete
samples.evidence: The design's cleanup table (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md, § Storage) commits to "Document deleted, **or workspace access lost** → Drop that entry", and `WafflebaseDocStore.purge`'s own doc comment repeats it (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:725-727: "the document was deleted, or workspace access was lost, and the content must not outlive the authority to read it"). Only the delete half is wired: `purgeOfflineDocuments` has exactly two call sites, `deleteDocument` (api/documents.ts:167) and `deleteDocuments` (api/documents.ts:215). Nothing hooks membership revocation (`api/workspaces.ts:98 removeMember`), role downgrade, or share-link revocation, and nothing reacts to a subsequent 403 on a document whose gzip'd full content is already in IndexedDB. Concretely: a contractor opens a sheet on their laptop with offline saving on, is removed from the workspace, and a complete plaintext-on-disk copy of that document (snapshot + change log, only gzip'd) remains readable via the app's own resume path and via devtools for up to 30 days, until `collectStale`'s `DefaultMaxAgeMs` sweep. That is exactly the "content outlives the authority to read it" condition the module says it prevents.

samples.summary: The share route's `NonDurableScope` guard does not cover the shared-PDF branch, which returns a `CollabDocumentProvider` above it
samples.evidence: `NonDurableScope` is opened at line 982, but `SharedDocumentInner` returns early at lines 933-946 for `kind === "pdf"`, rendering `SharedPdfLayout` → `PdfCollabProvider` → `CollabDocumentProvider` (app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199-200) entirely outside that scope, so `DurabilityPermitted` defaults to `true` (lib/use-durable-document.ts:60) on the public `/shared/:token` route. Today the durable branch is refused only by the unrelated `isExcluded(docKey)` prefix test (`docKey.startsWith("pdf-")`, use-durable-document.ts:39-41), which the design states is temporary ("PDF is excluded **until it has a chip**"). The moment that exclusion is lifted — a change nobody would expect to affect share links — a signed-in visitor on somebody else's share link gets the durable branch: their own `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` client authenticated with `fetchYorkieToken` (their personal token) instead of `fetchYorkieShareToken`, whose role/expiry the Yorkie auth webhook validates, plus the shared document's comment content written to their disk where the link's revocation cannot reach it. That is precisely the bypass the diff's own comment at line 973-981 says `NonDurableScope` exists to prevent, and the guard reads as route-wide while covering only one of the route's two provider paths. The gate is bypassable at a call site the guard's author believed it covered.

samples.summary: The logout erase is skipped when the logout request itself fails, which is the offline case this feature creates
samples.evidence: `logout()` rethrows from the `catch` at lines 94-98 when `fetch` rejects and `suppressFailure` is false — the default, and what `components/nav-user.tsx:41` uses — so `await eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` on line 105 never runs and `signedInUserId` is never consumed. The comment on 100-105 claims the erase is "never able to fail the sign-out itself", but the ordering means the reverse also holds: a failed sign-out silently skips the erase. The realistic sequence is the one this feature exists for: a user on a shared or borrowed machine with offline saving on goes offline, clicks Log out, sees an error, and closes the browser — leaving every persisted document (and archive) for that account on that disk for the full 30-day window, with no second attempt. Moving the erase above the `try`/`catch`, or into a `finally`, closes it.

samples.summary: Deleting a document purges only the deleting account's local copy, leaving other accounts' cached copies of a now-deleted document on the same device
samples.evidence: `purgeOfflineDocuments` constructs the store with `userId: signedInUserId` (line 99) and `WafflebaseDocStore.purgeDocument` filters candidates through `headerKeysWhere(BY_USER, IDBKeyRange.only(this.userId))` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:760-763). On a shared device where user B had also opened the document while it existed, B's full gzip'd snapshot and change log survive the deletion and remain loadable by B's own resume path until the 30-day sweep. The user-scoping is right for the *erase-on-logout* semantics but wrong here: the authority being withdrawn is the document's existence, which is not per-account. Lower severity than the revocation gap because both principals had legitimate read access at the time of caching, but it is the same class of "content outliving the authority to read it".

samples.summary: The offline IndexedDB database is created and opened for every authenticated user, including those who never opted in
samples.evidence: `OfflineRuntime` unconditionally constructs `new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId, ... })` (line 44) and calls `await store.collectStale()` (line 69) plus `offerRecoverableWork` (line 80) on every `PrivateRoute` mount, with no check of `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`. `collectStale` → `this.open()` → `indexedDB.open(this.dbName, DB_VERSION)`, which *creates* the `wafflebase-offline` database. So a user who has explicitly declined the per-device opt-in still has persistent origin storage provisioned on their machine by this feature. Nothing sensitive is written, but the feature's whole premise is that touching this device's disk is something the user consents to first; gating the sweep on the preference (or on the store being non-empty) would keep that promise exactly.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described. `collectStale` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:864-898) selects victims via `headerKeysWhere(BY_UPDATED_AT, range)` at :873 and `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` at :886, neither intersected with `BY_USER`; `dropArchivesWhere` (:973-988) deletes every id in the index range unconditionally, and `orphanSnapshotKeys` (:940-951) does a full-store `getAllKeys()`. The IndexedDB database is per-origin and shared across accounts (`DEFAULT_DB_NAME = "wafflebase-offline"` :35, `indexedDB.open(this.dbName, ...)` :330); identity exists only as a `userId` field/index on records (:349, :368). Every comparable path is deliberately user-scoped — `purgeDocument` :760-763, `listArchives` :787, `loadArchive` :811, `dropAllForUser` :843/:851, and notably `evictOldest` :1034-1036 which performs the exact `BY_USER` intersection `collectStale` lacks, with :1028-1033 explicitly naming the unscoped scan as a cross-account harm. The path is reachable in production: `OfflineRuntime` builds the store with the signed-in userId and awaits `store.collectStale()` on every mount (offline-runtime.tsx:44-51, :69), and it is rendered for every authenticated session from PrivateRoute.tsx:35. So user A signing in on a shared device destroys user B's aged headers and B's archives — the archives being, per this feature's design, the only copy of unreconciled work B would be offered back. No guard, caller-side check, or per-user DB separation makes this unreachable, and acting destructively on another account's records without authority is an access-control failure squarely in the security lane.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. Repo-wide grep shows purgeDocument/purgeOfflineDocuments has exactly two production callers (api/documents.ts:167 deleteDocument, :215 deleteDocuments) plus dropAllForUser on logout (api/auth.ts:105). No access-loss trigger exists anywhere: api/workspaces.ts:98 removeMember and api/share-links.ts:88 deleteShareLink do only the HTTP call; no 403 handler in the frontend purges local content; collectStale (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:864-898) is a pure age/orphan sweep with no server reconciliation; durable-yorkie-provider.tsx reacts only to local-changes-dropped and ErrDocumentOpenElsewhere; use-durable-document.ts gates eligibility only. Meanwhile the store's own contract (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:724-731, :743-757) and the design table (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:215) both commit to dropping the entry when workspace access is lost, so the local gzip'd snapshot + change log survives revocation until the 30-day sweep. Within the security lane as sensitive-data-at-rest outliving authorization. Two caveats that reduce blast radius but do not refute: share-link views are structurally excluded from persistence (use-durable-document.ts:43-69), so only workspace membership/role loss is affected; and the durable write path is currently dormant behind supportsClientKey() (yorkie-capabilities.ts:61-67, MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 vs pin 0.7.22 in package.json:65) — but the branch's own wiring note (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:242-246) says the dependency bump is meant to be the only remaining switch, so shipping this row missing means the bump alone enables the exposure.

finding.evidence: `NonDurableScope` is opened at line 982, but `SharedDocumentInner` returns early at lines 933-946 for `kind === "pdf"`, rendering `SharedPdfLayout` → `PdfCollabProvider` → `CollabDocumentProvider` (app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199-200) entirely outside that scope, so `DurabilityPermitted` defaults to `true` (lib/use-durable-document.ts:60) on the public `/shared/:token` route. The moment that exclusion is lifted — a change nobody would expect to affect share links — a signed-in visitor on somebody else's share link gets the durable branch: their own `wb:{userId}:{docKey}` client authenticated with `fetchYorkieToken` (their personal token) instead of `fetchYorkieShareToken`, whose role/expiry the Yorkie auth webhook validates, plus the shared document's comment content written to their disk where the link's revocation cannot reach it. That is precisely the bypass the diff's own comment at line 973-981 says `NonDurableScope` exists to prevent, and the guard reads as route-wide while covering only one of the route's two provider paths. verdict.reason: The structural observation is accurate — the `kind === "pdf"` early return (shared-document.tsx:933-946) does render `SharedPdfLayout` → `PdfCollabProvider` → `CollabDocumentProvider` (pdf-collab.tsx:199-200) outside the `NonDurableScope` opened at shared-document.tsx:982, so `DurabilityPermitted` is the default `true` (use-durable-document.ts:60). But the durable branch is unreachable on that path: `CollabDocumentProvider` only mounts `DurableYorkieProvider` with `fetchYorkieToken` when `durable && clientKey && me` (collab-document-provider.tsx:203-226), and `durable` requires `eligible`, which ANDs in `!isExcluded(docKey)` where `isExcluded` rejects every key beginning with `pdf-` (use-durable-document.ts:39-41, 115-120). The only collab provider anywhere inside the shared-PDF subtree is pdf-collab.tsx:199-200 with `docKey={`pdf-${documentId}`}` — I enumerated all `CollabDocumentProvider`/`DurableYorkieProvider` call sites in packages/frontend/src and there is no other provider under `SharedPdfLayout` (shared-document.tsx:718-758). The stale-election escape is also closed by the subject pairing (`durable = answered && !!decision?.session`, subject = `eligible\0userId\0docKey`, use-durable-document.ts:135,181-182), so a `pdf-` key cannot inherit an earlier document's durable session. Independently, the whole feature is opt-in and defaults off (offline-persistence-preference.ts:17). The reviewer's own chain is explicitly conditional on a future change ("the moment that exclusion is lifted"), so no signed-in visitor on a share link can obtain the personal-token durable client or local persistence of shared comment content in this tree. That makes it a defense-in-depth/guard-placement hardening item, not a live authorization or token-substitution bypass, and therefore not blocking under the Security rubric.

finding.summary: Share-link routes are not excluded from the durable path: the nested provider persists share-link content locally and re-authenticates the attach with the viewer's personal Yorkie token instead of the share token
finding.evidence: The design states share links are "excluded structurally" because `shared-document.tsx` mounts its own `YorkieProvider`. It does — but it mounts it ABOVE `CollabDocumentProvider` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:971-1042 renders `<YorkieProvider authTokenInjector={token ? () => fetchYorkieShareToken(token) : undefined}>` wrapping `<CollabDocumentProvider docKey={`doc-…`|`slides-…`|`note-…`|`board-…`|`sheet-…`} …>`). The new code in `CollabDocumentProvider` nests a `DurableYorkieProvider` INSIDE that, and `useDurableDocument` excludes only `docKey.startsWith('pdf-')` (packages/frontend/src/lib/use-durable-document.ts:31-33) — there is no share-route term. Attack/impact chain: a signed-in user opens a share link to a doc/slides/note/board/sheet; `useQuery(['me'], fetchMe)` resolves, `eligible` is true, the tab wins the election, and `CollabDocumentProvider` renders `<DurableYorkieProvider … authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken} …>` (collab-document-provider.tsx:184-197) with `WafflebaseDocStore` attached (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:76-96). Two security consequences: (a) the shared document's full content is written to that machine's IndexedDB and survives revocation/expiry of the share link — the design calls this exclusion a deliberate privacy decision ("the local copy then outlives the share link's revocation"); (b) the attach is re-credentialed with `fetchYorkieToken` (the account session token, api/auth.ts:238) rather than `fetchYorkieShareToken` (api/auth.ts:254, whose webhook "validates the wrapped share token (existence, expiry, role)"), so the share link's role and expiry stop governing that connection. Currently latent only because `supportsClientKey()` reads the `@yorkie-js/react` pin (0.7.22) and the gate opens at 0.7.23 — the task doc records that bumping the dependency is the entire switch, so this ships enabled on the next bump with no further review.

verdict.reason: The claimed absence of a share-route exclusion term is not what the code contains. `use-durable-document.ts:60` defines a `DurabilityPermitted` context and `:67-69` exports `NonDurableScope`; `permitted` is a conjunct of `eligible` at `:110` and `:115-120`, alongside the `pdf-` key exclusion. `shared-document.tsx:982` wraps every share-link document type in `<NonDurableScope>` (closing at `:1058`), positioned ABOVE the share-token `YorkieProvider` (`:983-990`) and therefore above all five `CollabDocumentProvider` mounts (`:992, 1011, 1020, 1035, 1048`) — the reviewer's cited range 971-1042 skips line 982. With `permitted` false, `durable` is false (`:182`) and `clientKey` undefined (`:198`), so `CollabDocumentProvider` returns the non-durable tree at `collab-document-provider.tsx:203-205` and never renders `DurableYorkieProvider` (`:207-226`) with `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}`. I enumerated the other share entry points: `SharedPdfLayout` (`shared-document.tsx:708-758`, reached via the early return at `:933-946`) uses `pdf-` keys already excluded by `isExcluded` (`use-durable-document.ts:39-41`), `SharedBlobLayout` mounts no Yorkie document (`:947-949`), and the template-gallery `/t/:id` embed flows through `SharedDocumentByToken` (`:1071`) → `SharedDocumentInner` (`:1133`), i.e. the same guarded path. No share-token call site reaches the durable branch unguarded, so neither asserted consequence (IndexedDB retention past revocation, re-credentialing with the personal token instead of `fetchYorkieShareToken`) is reachable.

finding.summary: No logout or access-revocation cleanup is wired, so document content this feature writes to disk outlives sign-out and outlives losing access to the document
finding.evidence: `dropAllForUser` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:795) and `purge` (line 717) exist but have no production caller: grepping `dropAllForUser|collectStale|purge(` across packages/frontend/src returns only the store, its tests, and `offline-erase.ts` (itself uncalled). `nav-user.tsx:40-42` logs out via `logout()` from `@/api/auth` with no offline erase, and `api/auth.ts`'s `logout` touches no IndexedDB. The design's cleanup table lists "Logout → drop every entry for that user" and "Document deleted, or workspace access lost → drop that entry" as required triggers, and `offline-erase.ts:66-70` even reasons on the assumption that "logout's own cleanup either ran" — it never runs. On a shared/borrowed machine (the exact threat model the opt-in is justified by) a signed-out user's document text, and the archives holding whole documents, remain readable in IndexedDB for up to 30 days, and content whose read authority was revoked is never purged. Latent while the version gate is closed, but it is the state the branch ships in.

verdict.reason: The claim that logout/access-revocation cleanup has "no production caller" is false. `logout()` in packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:105 awaits `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout()` (imported at auth.ts:4) before redirecting — that is the exact `logout` that nav-user.tsx:41 invokes, so the erase runs on sign-out; the reviewer inspected the call site but not the callee body. `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` (offline-erase.ts:65-79) calls `eraseOfflineData` → `store.dropAllForUser(who)` (offline-erase.ts:30), and `dropAllForUser` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:842-853) purges every user header entry AND `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, ...)` at :851, so the archives holding whole documents are erased too. The identity the erase needs is supplied in production: `rememberOfflineUser(userId)` at offline-runtime.tsx:42 (cleared at :89), and `OfflineRuntime` is mounted for all authenticated routes at PrivateRoute.tsx:35 — so the erase is not a silent no-op. Access-revocation-on-delete is likewise wired: api/documents.ts:6 imports `purgeOfflineDocuments`, invoked at documents.ts:167 (single delete) and documents.ts:215 (bulk delete, only for server-confirmed ids). The only residual gap is the narrower "workspace membership removed" trigger, which is a design-completeness concern distinct from the filed claim that no logout or access-revocation cleanup exists at all.
